clue.text: Bartender needing a wad chopped up for the plainest food

indicators.note: something chopped up is cut into bits and can be put back together in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barman wants a wad of something cut up to make the simplest possible meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread and water is the proverbial bare prison ration, the simplest diet a person could be given.

clue.text: Protective train buffer?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cushioning device on a railway carriage
setter's reading: a body of troops shielding the tail of an army's train of men and baggage

explanation.walkthrough: A train here is also the line of an army on the march, and the troops at its back protect it; the railway guard also rides at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard is the detachment of soldiers that protects the back of a marching army from attack.

clue.text: Anglo-Saxon writer trembles in the wind

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: the tree known for this

blocks.note: AS is the standard abbreviation for Anglo-Saxon
a pen is the tool that writes

explanation.surface: An Old English poet shivers out in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes rather than names: the aspen is the poplar whose leaves quiver in the slightest breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen poplar is famous for leaves on flattened stalks that shake and flutter in any light breeze.

clue.text: Brother got up after getting best bitter

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ace means first-rate, the best
BR is the abbreviation for brother

explanation.surface: A monk rose and drank the finest bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter looks like the beer, but it is the adjective; the brother's letters go after the best, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare synonym of acerbic, describing a sour, sharp taste or a harsh manner.

clue.text: Insignificant fellow spattered panda with dirt

indicators.note: spattered means splashed about, so these letters are scattered into new places

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some nobody flicked mud all over a panda.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandiprat is an old word for a dwarfish or worthless person, originally a small sixteenth-century coin.

clue.text: Incense in silver tomb, about a ton

indicators.note: about means going around, so the tomb wraps around what follows

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a grave is a burial place
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for ton

explanation.surface: Fragrant smoke drifts in a silver sepulchre, with a ton of it about.
explanation.walkthrough: Incense reads as the perfumed smoke, but it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them angry, and aggravate in everyday use means to annoy or exasperate.

clue.text: Actress Terry is well endowed, but not completely

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the answer sits inside it without its ends

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, dropping the outer letters

explanation.surface: A gossip remark that a famous actress is generously built, though not entirely so.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellen Terry was the leading Shakespearean actress of the Victorian London stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Ellen Terry was a celebrated English stage actress, so her first name fits the clue's description.

clue.text: Source named with all the necessary equipment

blocks.note: a well is a source of water
named to a post is appointed to it

explanation.surface: An informant has been identified and comes fully kitted out.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-appointed room or house is fully furnished and fitted out with everything required.

clue.text: Sarah concentrating on sauce

blocks.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
to address a task is to focus on it

explanation.surface: A woman named Sarah is focusing hard on making a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing such as vinaigrette is a cold liquid sauce poured over leaves and vegetables.

clue.text: Case of the former Liberal

blocks.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
liberal portions are generous, plentiful ones

explanation.surface: A political file on a one-time member of the Liberal Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes it look like the party; it is just generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point is an instance that illustrates something, the same sense as an example.

clue.text: Cookery writer knocks back gin with jazz singer

indicators.note: knocking something back sends it backwards, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
Ella Fitzgerald, the great jazz singer

explanation.surface: A food writer downs gin in the company of a jazz vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocks back looks like drinking; it turns the spirit around. Nigella Lawson is a well-known British food writer and TV cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella Lawson is a famous British author of cookbooks and presenter of television cooking programmes.

clue.text: American berry grower's moving along

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so these letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A US fruit farmer is making progress.
explanation.definitionFit: James Harvey Logan, an American judge and horticulturist, bred the loganberry, which bears his name.

clue.text: This female warrior's bust ain't in bra

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A cheeky line that a warrior woman's chest is not held in a brassiere.
explanation.walkthrough: Bust looks like the chest that suits the bra; it is the anagram signal. Britannia is the helmeted female figure personifying Britain, seen on old coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia is depicted as a woman warrior with helmet, shield and trident, the symbol of Britain.

clue.text: Midshipman called about the crash

blocks.note: read as mid-shipman: the middle letter of the seven-letter word inside it
rang means telephoned, called up

explanation.surface: A junior naval officer phoned to report the collision.
explanation.walkthrough: Midshipman looks like one officer, but it splits as mid + shipman, the centre letter of shipman. A prang is British slang for a minor car or aircraft crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is informal British slang for a collision or accident, especially a minor one involving a vehicle.

clue.text: Life in the fireplace and sink

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: a grate is the iron frame holding a fire
vita is Latin for life

explanation.surface: Domestic life centres on the hearth and the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: Sink looks like the kitchen fitting, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To gravitate is to move downward under gravity, so it can mean to settle or fall like something sinking.

clue.text: Encouraged to embrace a bishop when heckled

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping arms around, so the first word encloses the others

blocks.note: backed means supported or encouraged
taken as written
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A bishop is urged to hug people while being jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: Encouraged and heckled look like opposites in one scene; the first is wordplay, the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is British and Australian usage for jeering or shouting down a speaker or player.

clue.text: Standing place for objects with hard back and strange flesh

indicators.note: something strange is out of the normal, so these letters are set in an odd new order

blocks.note: a hardback is a bound volume with stiff covers
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A grisly description of something with a stiff back and weird flesh on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf for books is where volumes stand upright side by side, a place for things to stand.

clue.text: What the chef uses in a tense situation?

blocks.note: first meaning: the sharp side of a cook's blade
second meaning: a precarious state where things could go either way

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a cook in a crisis; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting side of a blade is its sharp edge, and being on a knife-edge means poised between success and disaster.

clue.text: Not even a soldier on strike could be called a misfit

blocks.note: a number not even is odd
a man is a soldier, as in officers and men
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: Not one soldier walking out on strike would be labelled an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd one out is the person who does not belong in a group, just as a misfit fails to fit in.

clue.text: The best of the Carmelites

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the answer is part of the word that follows

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: Praise for the finest of a Catholic order of friars and nuns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carmelites are a Roman Catholic religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite of a group are its most select and capable members, the pick of the bunch.

clue.text: Good-looking lad with scar and sinus damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A handsome boy whose face is marred by a scar and a bad nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus was the beautiful youth of Greek myth who fell in love with his own reflection.

clue.text: Cyclist's qualification

blocks.note: first meaning: someone on a bike
second meaning: an added clause limiting a statement or document

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a cyclist's certificate; the possessive just joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on a bicycle is a rider, and a rider is also an extra condition attached to a contract or verdict.

clue.text: She keeps us in the sanatorium

indicators.note: one thing in another is held inside it

blocks.note: san is a short form of sanatorium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A matron keeps us confined to the sickbay.
explanation.walkthrough: She looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition: any woman's name fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a woman's name, and crosswords use she to define a female first name.

clue.text: Praise for Elizabeth when going round the lake

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it

blocks.note: Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Applause for a woman named Elizabeth as she walks around the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless God is to praise or glorify him, as in hymns and psalms.

clue.text: English poet and artist born over the water

blocks.note: b. is the abbreviation for born
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: An English painter-poet was born across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Over looks like across the sea; in a down entry it means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: William Blake was an English Romantic poet who also engraved and painted his own illustrated books.

clue.text: Final stage when death reaches wild animals for sport

blocks.note: death is one's end
game is wild animals hunted for sport

explanation.surface: The last phase of a hunt, when death comes to the quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the last phase of a chess match, and by extension the closing stage of any process.

clue.text: Nearly suffering as a substitute

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to stand something is to put up with it

explanation.surface: Someone almost in pain while filling in for another.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in takes another person's place, like an actor's double or a temporary replacement.

clue.text: Envious, getting identified as Charlie Dimmock

definitions.note: a person standing for the adjective that describes her

blocks.note: green with envy
to finger a suspect is to identify them

explanation.surface: A jealous person is named as a TV celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Dimmock is a British TV gardener from Ground Force; she is an example of the quality, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Green-fingered means skilled at growing plants, exemplified by a television gardening presenter famous for garden makeovers.
